problem: LLM-based zero-shot VLN-CE agents lack fine-grained spatial perception, so they fail on door interaction (door state/orientation), multi-room transitions and landmark-sparse ambiguous instructions. Single-view 2D semantic recognition is inconsistent and gives no explicit 3D or region structure.
motivation: Simple commands like 'go through the door into the living room' fail when several doors are visible. The cause is missing spatial awareness, not semantic misunderstanding. Explicit spatial perception plus active resolution of ambiguity should improve robustness in simulation and on real robots.
key_idea: Enhance perception with panoramic-consistency filtering and door/region experts, then run waypoint-level and region-level LLM experts in parallel, triggering active exploration when their decisions conflict.
insight: The ablation shows neither module alone is sufficient: on the door and ambiguous-instruction tasks, exploration-based reasoning (EMR only) beats perception only (SPE only) by 4 and 3 SR points. Both variants still trail the full model, so exploration needs perceptual grounding. Multi-region tasks stay hard (both single-module variants at 15% SR, full model 16%), which points to long-term memory and progress estimation as the bottleneck. Structured spatial perception lets cheap LLMs (Gemma-27B, GPT-OSS-20B) beat Open-Nav with GPT-4.
method: Consistency check: RAM and SpatialBot give per-view semantics and spatial relations. Views are stitched into 4 regional panoramas (90° each), and a filtering expert discards single-view semantics that disagree with the panorama semantics.
Regional perception: dual-scale history experts, one for the waypoint level and one for the region level, update history states to track region transitions and orientation changes.

Multi-modal door perception: door candidates from semantics (ROI, distance, appearance) are cross-checked against LiDAR geometric openings from depth discontinuities. Matched doors are 'open', others 'closed', and the room or furniture behind an open door is recognized.

Multi-scale dual-expert reasoning: the instruction is decomposed into waypoint and region sub-task sequences. Progress-estimation experts and separate waypoint and region action experts each propose a decision.

Conflict-driven exploration: if the predicted waypoint does not lie in the predicted region, an exploration expert picks a region, and the agent goes to a waypoint there (or a LiDAR frontier). It then re-decides with the augmented observations.

Value-based waypoint sampling (real world): a polar grid (120x12, 3 m range) is scored as free-space occupancy times a RAM semantic-richness weight. Distant high-score cells are sampled, adjacent candidates merged, and random diverse points added.
Low-level controller: a DRL policy (TDANet-style) retrained with LiDAR plus depth-derived obstacle maps outputs continuous velocity commands.

setting.backbone: Frozen LLM experts (DeepSeek-v3 API, GPT-OSS-20B, Gemma-27B, Llama3.1-70B, Qwen2-72B, Phi3-14B, Doubao-1.5) with RAM and SpatialBot perception; DRL controller for real-world low-level control
setting.training_data: none (training-free for the navigation decisions; only the real-world DRL local controller is retrained)
setting.observation: 12-view panoramic RGB-D (30° spacing) plus LiDAR occupancy map, with position tracking
setting.action_space: Low-level FORWARD 0.25 m / TURN 15° / STOP in simulation, executed via selected candidate waypoints; continuous velocity commands from a DRL controller in the real world

results: Spatial-VLN with DeepSeek-v3 reaches 33% SR and 27.44 SPL on VLN-CE unseen. This beats Open-Nav-GPT4 (19 SR), SmartWay-GPT4o (29 SR) and CA-Nav-GPT4 (25.3 SR), but not the supervised ETPNav (52 SR). On the hard challenge subsets it improves over Open-Nav by 12 SR on doors and 13 SR on ambiguous instructions. Real-world SR reaches 44% in offices and 52% in homes versus 28% and 34% for Open-Nav.
limitations: Long-horizon multi-room navigation improves only marginally (SR 14→16) because of weak long-term memory and progress estimation.
Multi-expert LLM calls, panoramic stitching and exploration are costly; the absolute zero-shot SR (33%) still lags supervised methods (ETPNav 52%).
Evaluation subsets are small (100 episodes for the challenge sets, 40 real-world instructions), and the real-world results are limited to two scene types.
